description: We are a multidisciplinary team passionate about healthcare, pharmaceutical sciences, and space exploration. We aim to develop innovative, science-driven solutions to address real challenges faced by astronauts during long-duration space missions. We believe that combining medical knowledge, teamwork, and technology can help create smarter approaches to astronaut health monitoring and support future space exploration.
summary:
AstroGuard is an integrated astronaut health-monitoring software prototype developed by Team NovaPharma for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It brings seven health domains into one platform, using individual baselines to track changes, visualize health trends, and identify potential concerns. The platform features a Mission Control dashboard, an interactive Digital Twin, an Alerts Center, an Action Center for structured follow-up, scenario comparisons, and AURA, a rule-based digital companion.

AstroGuard addresses the challenge by connecting health indicators into a clearer, more explainable monitoring workflow: Monitor, Analyze, Visualize, and Respond. This is important because long-duration space missions expose astronauts to multiple interacting health risks, making continuous awareness and timely follow-up essential. The current prototype uses simulated data and is designed to support not replacemedical teams.
details:
AstroGuard is a browser-based astronaut health-monitoring platform designed to support crew health awareness during long-duration space missions.

It monitors seven health domains using simulated crew data and individual baselines to identify changes over time. Its features include a Mission Control dashboard, health analytics, an interactive Digital Twin, an Alerts Center, an Action Center for structured follow-up, scenario comparisons, and AURA, a rule-based digital companion.

The platform follows a Monitor, Analyze, Visualize, and Respond workflow. It helps users explore health trends, understand potential concerns, and organize follow-up actions. Its intended impact is to support earlier awareness of changing health patterns and improve communication between astronauts and medical teams.

AstroGuard was developed using JavaScript, React, and ES modules, with esbuild for bundling into a self-contained HTML application. Its Digital Twin uses a custom WebGL2 renderer. Node.js and Playwright were used for testing, while GitHub and Vercel supported source control and deployment. No dedicated hardware is required for the current prototype.

The project's creativity lies in combining personalized baselines, multi-domain monitoring, explainable alerts, interactive visualization, and structured follow-up in one platform. The team considered spaceflight health risks, data reliability, usability, scientific accuracy, and the limitations of simulated data.

AI Declaration: AI tools, including ChatGPT and Claude, were used to assist with research organization, brainstorming, coding, debugging, documentation, and content refinement. The team reviewed and refined AI-assisted outputs and remains responsible for the final project and its submitted materials.
